primary_text:
My roommate is a hafiz. So when he walked into the kitchen at 1 AM, I flipped my phone face down so fast I almost knocked my mug off the counter.
1:14 AM on a Tuesday, to be exact.
Bilal stood in the doorway, squinting at the light.
I am 27. I have a job, a lease, a dying houseplant.
And I was hiding my phone screen like a kid caught cheating on a test.
Bilal looked at the phone. Then at me.
"Bro. What are you doing?"
It was not a girl. It was not gambling. It was nothing you would guess.
On my screen was a Google search.
The English translation of a verse I have recited thousands of times since before I was ten.
[... long-form first-person story, 8,068 characters in total; truncated in this record. Beats: dad asks him to lead Eid prayer; 'I can recite beautifully... And I understood almost none of it'; street-signs analogy; 'Just 500 words make up about 75% of the entire Quran'; spiral-bound book, two words per page, five minutes a day; honest diary week 1 / week 4; led Eid prayer; 'Your prayer has always counted, in sha Allah. You were never faking it. Nobody ever taught you the words. That is not your fault.'; 'There is a 30-day money-back guarantee, so the only thing you are risking is five minutes a day.'; 'Every order sends a meal to Palestine.'; scarcity 'the print version is really limited'. Link: https://yaqeenbooks.com/products/the-top-500-words-in-the-quran-physical-book-bonuses]
headline: I recited the Quran for 20 years without understanding it
